megabooks.title: The Odyssey
megabooks.author: Homer
megabooks.description: Homer's epic of return, compiled here from six pre-1929 printings digitized by the Library of Congress: the classic Butcher & Lang prose translation, a Victorian verse rendering, the ancient Greek of the Phaeacian books, John Flaxman's celebrated illustrated edition, a scholarly companion, and a children's retelling. One work, many doors in.

components.title: The Odyssey of Homer (prose)
components.contributor: Trans. S. H. Butcher & Andrew Lang
components.note: The standard prose translation of its era — the version most English readers of the early 20th century knew.

components.title: The Odyssey (verse)
components.note: A Victorian rendering in dramatic blank verse — read it against Butcher & Lang to feel how much a translator's choices shape the poem.

components.title: The Phæacian Episode (Books VI–VIII, XIII)
components.note: The ancient Greek text of the Phaeacian books with 19th-century scholarly apparatus. Presented as page facsimiles — OCR does not survive polytonic Greek.

components.title: The Odyssey, with Flaxman's Designs
components.contributor: Trans. T. A. Buckley · Ill. John Flaxman
components.note: John Flaxman's neoclassical outline engravings — among the most influential Homer illustrations ever made. Browse as facsimile plates.

components.title: Homer: The Odyssey (Ancient Classics for English Readers)
components.note: A compact Victorian companion — plot, composition, and context in 156 pages. A good first door into the epic.

components.title: The Children's Odyssey
components.contributor: Told from Homer in simple language
components.note: The epic retold for young readers — a reminder that every generation rebuilds Homer for itself.

megabooks.title: The Bible
megabooks.description: Scripture as a megabook: the King James text beside a monumental Victorian variorum apparatus, Gustave Doré's complete engravings, and the Greek New Testament of Westcott & Hort — the critical edition that changed biblical scholarship. Four doors into the most-printed book on earth.

components.title: The Holy Bible, King James Version
components.note: The 1611 Authorized Version as the 19th century read it — the base text of English-speaking scripture.

components.title: The Variorum Teacher's Bible
components.note: Nearly 2,000 pages: the KJV with variant readings and renderings from dozens of scholars compiled verse by verse — a megabook avant la lettre.

components.title: The Doré Bible Gallery
components.note: Doré's celebrated engravings with facing descriptions — the images that fixed the Bible's look in the popular imagination.

components.title: The New Testament in the Original Greek
components.note: The landmark 1881 critical Greek text, built from the oldest manuscripts.

megabooks.title: Paradise Lost
megabooks.author: John Milton
megabooks.description: Milton's epic of the Fall in three printings across half a century — read the poem plain, annotated, and in the company of his complete poetical works.

components.title: Paradise Lost: A Poem in Twelve Books
components.note: A clean mid-century reading text of the twelve books.

components.title: The Paradise Lost
components.note: A fuller apparatus edition — useful against the 1852 for how editors dressed the poem.

components.title: The Poetical Works of John Milton
components.note: The epic in context: Paradise Regained, Samson Agonistes, and the shorter poems alongside.

megabooks.title: The Arabian Nights
megabooks.description: The Thousand and One Nights in three early-20th-century printings — tale against tale across editions, including a hundred-illustration edition from 1924.

components.title: The Arabian Nights
components.note: An Edwardian reading edition of the Nights.

components.title: The Arabian Nights' Entertainments
components.note: The Nights under their classic English title.

components.title: The Arabian Nights, with One Hundred Illustrations
components.note: A hundred plates woven through the tales — compare its choices against the plain texts.

megabooks.title: Leaves of Grass
megabooks.author: Walt Whitman
megabooks.description: One poem, growing. Whitman revised Leaves of Grass his whole life — this megabook shelves three printings spanning a quarter century, so the layers are not translations but time itself.

components.title: Leaves of Grass (1897)
components.note: Printed just after Whitman's death — the 'deathbed' arrangement he authorized.

components.title: Leaves of Grass (1900)
components.note: A turn-of-the-century printing of the completed book.

components.title: Leaves of Grass (1921)
components.note: The poem as the modernists inherited it.

megabooks.title: Acâibü'l-Mahlûkât · The Book of Wonders
megabooks.author: Zakariyyā al-Qazwīnī
megabooks.description: Qazwīnī's 13th-century cosmography — angels, constellations, seas, beasts, and marvels — travelled the Islamic world in translation. Here it is as illuminated manuscript in Ottoman Turkish (1553) and Persian (1565), and as a 19th-century Persian lithograph. The Ottoman manuscript also carries oedio's first complete AI transcription and translation — all 314 pages rendered into readable text and English, likely for the first time.

components.title: ʻAjāʾib al-makhlūqāt — Ottoman Turkish manuscript
components.note: The Ottoman Turkish translation, copied 1553 — miniatures and illumination throughout.

components.title: ʻAjāʾib al-makhlūqāt — Persian manuscript
components.note: A 713-page Persian manuscript of the Wonders, richly illustrated.

components.title: ʻAjāʾib al-makhlūqāt — Persian lithograph
components.note: The Wonders in print: a 19th-century lithographed edition with drawn illustrations.

components.title: ʻAjāʾib al-makhlūqāt — Ottoman text (AI transcription)
components.contributor: Transcribed from the 1553 manuscript by Claude (AI)
components.note: A complete AI transcription of the manuscript's nesih hand into readable Arabic-script text, all 314 pages, beside the original scans — unverified, and offered so readers can check it against the source.

components.title: The Wonders of Creation — English (AI translation)
components.contributor: Translated from the Ottoman Turkish by Claude (AI)
components.note: The first known English rendering of this Ottoman translation, all 314 pages — generated by AI from the manuscript itself, unverified, with the source scan one tap away on every page.
